captions.apple: This picture shows the fruit apple, not the technology company. Notice the skin, flesh and stalk.
captions.banana: Connect banana with the shape of the fruit, then learn expressions such as a banana and banana peel.
captions.orange: The picture shows orange as a fruit. The word can also name the colour orange.
captions.pear: Look at the shape of a pear, then connect it with other fruit words such as apple and peach.
captions.lemon: A lemon is a citrus fruit. You can also learn the expression lemon juice.
captions.grape: One individual fruit is a grape; several growing together form a bunch of grapes.
captions.strawberry: This picture shows the fruit strawberry. Its plural form is strawberries.
captions.pineapple: A pineapple is the fruit shown here. Its meaning cannot be guessed simply by combining the usual modern meanings of pine and apple.
captions.watermelon: Recognise a watermelon from the real fruit, and connect its rind, flesh and seeds in one scene.
captions.peach: The picture illustrates peach as a fruit. Compare its shape with a pear or an apple.
captions.cherry: A cherry is the fruit shown here; the plural form is cherries.
captions.mango: This picture shows a mango, the fruit, rather than a brand with the same name.
captions.dog: This is the common animal meaning of dog, not a specialised meaning such as a support for logs in a fireplace.
captions.cat: The picture shows cat as an animal. Learn it together with the expression a pet cat.
captions.rabbit: Notice the rabbit's ears and overall shape, and connect the word with the animal itself.
captions.horse: A horse is the animal shown here. Connect the picture with the action in ride a horse.
captions.sheep: Sheep is the same form for one animal and for more than one.
captions.goat: Compare the appearance of a goat and a sheep instead of learning only their similar Chinese category names.
captions.tiger: The tiger's stripes help connect the word with the animal's appearance.
captions.lion: This picture shows a lion, the animal, rather than a person or brand with the same name.
captions.deer: Deer names the animal; its singular and plural forms have the same spelling.
captions.fox: Fox here means the animal, not a media brand with the same name.
captions.wolf: This picture shows wolf as an animal. The plural form is wolves.
captions.bird: Bird is a general name for the animal group; the photograph shows an example from that group.
captions.fish: The picture shows fish as an animal. Fish can also be a verb meaning to catch fish.
captions.butterfly: Recognise a butterfly by the shape of its wings. The plural form is butterflies.
captions.bee: This picture shows the insect bee. Do not confuse the animal with the letter B.
captions.ant: Notice the small insect's appearance to connect ant with the animal, not just its Chinese translation.
captions.spider: Spider here means the animal, not a web crawler in computing.
captions.turtle: The picture shows turtle as an animal. Notice features such as its shell.
captions.frog: Frog names this kind of animal; the image helps distinguish it from other small animals.
captions.flower: A flower is part of a flowering plant. Flower can also be a verb in an appropriate context.
captions.tree: This picture shows the plant meaning of tree, not a tree-shaped data structure in computing.
captions.leaf: Leaf names a plant leaf. The plural form is leaves.
captions.rose: Rose here names a flower. It can also be the past tense of rise, depending on the context.
captions.seed: Connect a seed with the growth of a plant and its flowers by looking at the real object.
captions.cactus: The picture shows an example of the plants called cacti.
captions.mushroom: The picture illustrates the word mushroom; it must not be used to decide whether a wild fungus is safe to eat.
captions.table: This picture shows table as furniture. It does not illustrate meanings such as a data table or a list.
captions.chair: Chair here means a seat; other uses, such as chairing a meeting, depend on context.
captions.book: The photograph shows the noun book. In book a room, book is a verb meaning to reserve.
captions.pencil: Compare a pencil with a pen in appearance and use.
captions.pen: Pen here means a writing instrument. The picture does not represent every kind of pen.
captions.spoon: Learn spoon together with fork and plate as part of a dining scene.
captions.plate: The picture shows plate as tableware. Learn the expression put food on a plate.
captions.kettle: A kettle is used for boiling water; it is not the same as a cup or a bottle for holding water.
captions.bottle: A bottle is a container; a bottle of water means water held in one bottle.
captions.cup: This picture shows cup as a drinking vessel. Uses as a unit of measurement need their own context.
captions.umbrella: Connect an umbrella with the situation in which it is used on a rainy day.
captions.clock: Clock usually names a timepiece such as the one shown here. A timepiece worn on the wrist is normally called a watch.
captions.scissors: The usual expression for one cutting tool of this kind is a pair of scissors.
captions.backpack: A backpack is carried on the back. Notice its shoulder straps.
captions.ladder: Connect a ladder's rungs with the action of climbing upwards.
captions.hammer: Hammer here names the tool. It can also be a verb meaning to strike with a hammer.
captions.telescope: A telescope helps you observe distant objects. Compare its purpose with that of a microscope.
captions.microscope: A microscope is used to examine very small objects; the picture shows this kind of instrument.
captions.compass: This compass is used to find directions, not to draw circles.
captions.candle: Connect a candle with the expression light a candle.
captions.wheel: The image links a wheel with vehicles and the action of turning.
captions.bicycle: Connect a bicycle's wheels and frame with the activity of riding it.
captions.piano: Piano here names the instrument, not the musical instruction to play softly.
captions.violin: Notice the violin's body, strings and bow.
captions.train: The picture shows train as a means of transport. The verb train means to teach or practise a skill.
captions.bus: This is the vehicle meaning of bus, not the computing term for a system connection.
captions.camera: A camera records images. The photograph shows a concrete device rather than an abstract technology.
captions.computer: This picture of a personal computer illustrates the common device meaning of computer.
captions.keyboard: The picture shows a computer keyboard, not the keyboard of a musical instrument.
captions.mountain: Connect mountain with the landscape rather than learning only a single translated word.
captions.river: River names a natural watercourse; the photograph shows a geographical scene.
captions.waterfall: This is a waterfall in nature, not the waterfall model of software development.
captions.island: An island is land surrounded by water; the landscape makes the meaning visible.
captions.volcano: The picture shows a volcano as a landform; it does not mean that the volcano is always erupting.
captions.rainbow: The image illustrates the natural phenomenon called a rainbow.
captions.cloud: This is a cloud in the sky, not a cloud-computing service.
captions.forest: Connect forest with the whole environment formed by many trees together.
captions.desert: This is the geographical noun desert. The verb has a different meaning and pronunciation.
captions.beach: A beach is a stretch of shore beside the sea or another body of water. Learn it with sea and sand.
captions.ocean: Ocean names a large body of salt water. The image shows a geographical environment, not a particular country.
captions.moon: Moon here refers to Earth's Moon.
captions.sun: The picture shows the Sun, a star, and helps connect sun with words such as sunlight.
captions.water: The picture shows drinking water. In water the plants, water instead names the action of giving plants water.
captions.coffee: The picture shows coffee as a drink. Learn it with the expression a cup of coffee.
captions.house: This detached home illustrates house as a building, not other meanings involving organisations or institutions.
captions.rain: Rain here names a natural weather phenomenon. It can also be used as a verb.
captions.snow: The photograph illustrates snow as a natural phenomenon, not every figurative use of the word.
captions.photograph: A photograph records an image formed by light; photo- relates to light and -graph relates to recording.
captions.photographer: A photographer uses a camera to take photographs. The picture shows this occupation at work.
captions.microphone: A microphone converts sound into signals that can be processed, transmitted or recorded.
captions.telephone: A telephone enables people in different places to talk to one another. The picture shows the equipment.
captions.aquarium: An aquarium is a water-filled container for keeping or displaying aquatic animals and plants. The word can also name a public aquarium.
captions.aqueduct: An aqueduct carries water from one place to another through a channel or a bridge-like structure.
captions.photosynthesis: The diagram illustrates how green plants and other organisms use light energy to make organic substances.
captions.architecture: Architecture involves designing and constructing buildings; it can also refer to their overall style.
captions.construction: Construction combines materials and components to build facilities such as houses and roads.
captions.structure: The DNA double helix illustrates structure: how parts are arranged and connected to make a whole.
captions.transport: Transport moves people or things from one place to another. The picture illustrates that activity.
captions.processor: A processor is an electronic component that handles data according to instructions. The picture shows a computer processor.
captions.submarine: A submarine is a vessel that can travel underwater; sub- is associated with being under or below.
captions.airport: An airport is a place where aircraft take off and land and where passenger or cargo transport is handled.
captions.thermometer: A thermometer measures temperature; thermo- relates to heat and -meter to measurement.
captions.photocopy: The picture shows a photocopier to illustrate photocopy as either a copy or the action of making one.
captions.reflection: Reflection occurs when light or another wave meets a boundary and returns to its original medium. The word can also mean a reflected image or careful thought.
captions.recycling: The recycling symbol uses arrows in a loop to suggest collecting, processing and reusing materials.
captions.portable: The laptop illustrates something that can be carried relatively easily. Portable is an adjective.
captions.export: The shipping scene illustrates export: selling or sending goods to another country.
captions.import: The cargo port illustrates import: buying or bringing goods in from another country.
captions.battery: A battery stores chemical energy and provides electrical energy.
captions.electricity: Electricity concerns electric charge and its movement. The picture illustrates a related physical phenomenon.
captions.microscopic: A microscope provides a scene for understanding microscopic. The adjective describes something extremely small or visible only through a microscope.
captions.telescopic: The equipment illustrates the telescope-related meaning of telescopic. Other meanings, such as extendable, depend on context.
captions.photographic: The sample photograph illustrates the photography-related meaning of photographic.
captions.photography: A photograph is the result of photography, which can mean the technique, process or art of taking photographs.
captions.construct: The construction scene illustrates the action construct, meaning to build.
captions.constructor: The construction scene illustrates a person or organisation that builds. A constructor in programming belongs to a different domain.
captions.transportation: The transport scene illustrates moving people or things from one place to another.
captions.recycle: The looping arrows of the recycling symbol suggest recovering materials and using them again.
captions.recyclable: The recycling scene illustrates recyclable: capable of being processed and used again.
captions.reflect: This picture illustrates reflecting light or an image. Reflect can also mean to think carefully.
captions.aquatic: Organisms in an aquarium illustrate aquatic, meaning living or growing in water.
captions.computerize: The computer equipment illustrates using computers to do work that was previously done manually.
captions.cyclist: The bicycle helps connect cyclist with the person who rides it.
captions.photocopying: A photocopier is the equipment used to carry out the action of photocopying.
